rv.q: Jordan Fein’s magical production of Sondheim and James Lapine’s fairytale meta-mash-up is even better than ever.
Now it’s crossed the river to the Noël Coward with a mostly new cast, and it’s every bit as good.
Fein and Scutt’s supernaturally good mix of the dark and the light ensures its spell never breaks.
Fein has created a production that has magic and drama, danger and hope, and is sinister and illusory all at once.
A production that has lost none of its magic.
This return to the woods is not to be missed.
As well as being thrilling, it also reminds us we will leave the theatre after the show and return to the real world.
Into the Woods, let's dare to state it, is the most perfect music-theatre creation of the last 40 years.
Jordan Fein's direction has injected humour and charm into the musical with a few necessary twists of the macabre.
All things considered, it’s a very satisfying and gritty show, with touches of lighthearted silliness in amongst the doom and gloom.
This is not merely an outstanding revival of a musical masterpiece.
It is a stirring and stunning production that I am proud to say has survived its transfer, and truly is, in my opinion, a perfect production of a perfect musical.
An unforgettable show that I wouldn't even hesitate in giving 5 stars to, not one moment of hesitation at all.
It’s theatre at its absolute finest.
Jordan Fein’s glorious new production will, I think, convert many a Sondheim-sceptic to go deeper into his ironic brilliant darkness and depth, at least for this show.

Transferring from the wide open spaces of the Bridge Theatre to the more traditional end-on setting of a traditional proscenium arch theatre like the Noël Coward has resulted in a tighter, funnier and ultimately even more satisfying production of Into the Woods.
Into the Woods is a masterful production, trusting its script, performers and audience, resulting in a production for the ages.
Theatre’s revival of Stephen Sondheim and James Lapine’s masterpiece was magnificent.
It’s a sight to behold with an extraordinary cast, and you leave with a smile on your face.
A luscious and hugely entertaining Olivier Award-winning production of Sondheim’s musical, giving familiar fairy tales an adult makeover.
Moments in the woods will surely make the children listen.
Fleetwood’s Witch and Pitt-Pulford’s Baker’s Wife make Sondheim’s dark fairytale utterly unmissable.
Together they confirm him as one of the most substantial talents in theatre today, able to get to the heart of a work and make it shine.
For fans of Sondheim musicals, this production of Into The Woods would certainly be one to go and see.
Overall, Into the Woods is an incredible must-see show, ticking all the elements of a great night out!
The Woods maxes out on meta gameplay in this technically brilliant but at times baseless musical that can be terribly proud of itself.
This is an astonishing piece of theatre that highlights every note, cadence and inflection of Sondheim’s extraordinary score.
Simply stunning from start to finish.
These are woods you’ll want to get lost in; just remember to drop your breadcrumbs.
Jordan Fein's production succeeds in capturing the complexity of this musical that makes it so enduring.
Audiences may not find themselves home before dark on the ever-shortening days, but what remains is a journey of a musical epic that continues to thrill.
This is a tight production in all the positive ways.

cn.t: This Olivier-winning revival casts a spell with its magical staging and stellar performances, particularly Kate Fleetwood's Witch. Critics praise Fein's intimate, witty production as a triumphant West End transfer of Sondheim's dark fairytale masterpiece.
